solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wave from lecturer during period around teatime, say

indicators.note: during says the lecturer's letter sits within the stretch of time

parts.note: four-ish, roughly four o'clock, is when afternoon tea is taken

explanation.surface: A lecturer waves while taking a break for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period around teatime' is FOURISH, about four o'clock, the British hour for afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish is a showy waving movement, as of a hand or a sword, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Female having more unusual stuff to eat

parts.note: odder means stranger, more unusual

explanation.surface: A woman with peculiar tastes picks strange food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is feed for livestock, loosely any food, hence stuff to eat.

clue.text: Exposed leading journalist who had nothing to write at the beginning

indicators.note: at the beginning puts the nought and the writing word ahead of the journalist

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for nothing
to pen is to write
ED, the editor, is the newspaper's leading journalist

explanation.surface: A top journalist with a blank page is shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' reads like a scandal about the journalist, but it is the definition; 'at the beginning' moves the nothing-and-writing pieces to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Opened, as in laid open or uncovered, works as a synonym of exposed.

clue.text: Unexpectedly subeditor is leaving fieldwork

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals that the letters come out in an unforeseen order
leaving says the letters of the little word are taken away from the longer one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A subeditor quits the office without warning to go and work in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I and S out of SUBEDITOR, and 'Unexpectedly' rearranges the remaining UBEDTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary earthwork fortification, a military fieldwork in the strict sense.

clue.text: Press in and win narrowly

definitions.meaning: to force something into place by pressing tightly
to scrape a victory, just getting across the line first

explanation.surface: Journalists crowd in as someone just edges a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to push something firmly into a space and to win a race by a whisker.

clue.text: Wealthy elite's rapid transport prepared

parts.note: a jet aircraft is a fast means of travel
set means ready, prepared

explanation.surface: The rich have their private jets standing by.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are the fashionable rich who fly around the world for pleasure.

clue.text: Sweep vessels into river

indicators.note: into says the cooking vessels go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: Boats sweep into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' looks like ships but means cooking pots.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide open stretch, as is a sweep of land or sea.

clue.text: Notice cut when it moved up and down

parts.note: to notice is to see
sawed means cut with a saw

explanation.surface: Someone sees a log being sawn while it bobs about.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesawed means rocked alternately up and down, like the playground plank.

clue.text: Number one even at the highest plane

parts.note: the top spot in the charts is number one
level means even, flat

explanation.surface: The leader stays steady while flying highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something top-level is at the highest rank or tier, here called a plane.

clue.text: Drive feudal reform that is unpleasant

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive

indicators.note: reform means re-form, so the letters of the old social system are shaped anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A campaign to overhaul feudalism that proves nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful is a common synonym for very unpleasant or bad.

clue.text: Maintenance of stronghold mounting in advance

indicators.note: in advance puts the riding word in front of the castle word

parts.note: up means on horseback, mounted
a keep is the central stronghold of a castle

explanation.surface: Repairs to a castle are lined up early.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair, its maintenance.

clue.text: Quartet leaving director to sign legal document

indicators.note: leaving says the foursome walks out of the boardroom figure

parts.note: an executive is a company director
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four members quit the board so a contract can be signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quartet' looks like musicians but is the number four, IV in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a deed or contract is to sign it formally so it takes legal effect.

clue.text: Need time in Oxfordshire

parts.note: want means need, lack
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone needs to spend time in Oxfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: WANTAGE is a market town in Oxfordshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantage is a town in that county, so the place is described by its location.

clue.text: Forecaster's craft?

parts.note: craft reads as skill, but here a vessel: a boat stationed at sea to make meteorological observations

explanation.surface: A question about the skill of predicting the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a ship was kept at sea to report conditions for meteorologists, literally the forecaster's vessel.

clue.text: It is used unspectacularly for seeing

definitions.text: It is used unspectacularly for seeing

parts.words: It is used unspectacularly for seeing
parts.note: unspectacularly reads as dully, but means without spectacles: vision with no glasses or telescope

explanation.surface: Something dull that helps us see.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaided vision, without lenses or instruments, is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: A fool giving support to communist opinions

parts.note: git is British slang for a stupid person
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: An idiot backs Marxist views.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop was Soviet political propaganda, communist views pushed through art and literature.

clue.text: Musical choirman's out of tune

indicators.note: out of tune means not right, so the singer's letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chorister is singing off key.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonic means relating to harmony, hence musical in a sense.

clue.text: Good to adopt as son or daughter an older person!

parts.note: grand means very good, splendid

parts.words: to adopt as son or daughter
parts.note: to mother someone is to care for them as your own child

explanation.surface: A kindly older figure takes in a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to mother' rather than 'to father' fixes the gender of the senior relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The adopter's own parent is a generation above, an older person indeed.

clue.text: Soaked bed left trail

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letters of the sleeping place go from the longer word

parts.note: bedraggled means wet through and dishevelled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sodden bed leaves a trail behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes B, E from the front and D from the end of BEDRAGGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To draggle is to trail along the ground, getting wet and dirty.

clue.text: Rogers' weight in Hertfordshire

parts.note: Roy Rogers was the singing cowboy of films, so his possession is Roy's
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone named Rogers has some heft in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: ROYSTON is a town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London; Roy Rogers was a Hollywood cowboy star.
explanation.definitionFit: Royston is a town in that county, so it is described by its location.

clue.text: More productive kitchen utensil husband included

indicators.note: included says the husband's letter goes inside the gadget

parts.note: a ricer presses cooked potatoes into fine strands

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget with a husband added makes for more output.
explanation.definitionFit: Richer soil or land is more fertile, yielding more produce.

clue.text: Standing sculptures English cast aside

indicators.note: cast aside means thrown away, so the country letter is removed

parts.note: statues are sculptures

explanation.surface: Standing statues, with English ones thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' tempts as a sculptor's term, but 'cast aside' only removes a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing as in social position or rank is a synonym of status.

clue.text: Tamil be preparing dish with mould!

indicators.note: preparing suggests making something up, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tamil cook gets a moulded dish ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a dish cooked in a drum-shaped mould, or the mould itself.

clue.text: Beat, half of this removed first by versifier

indicators.note: removed says those letters are taken out of the beat word

parts.note: rhythm is a musical beat

indicators.note: half of takes the front two of the four letters

parts.note: 1st, written IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A poet's rhythm is half cut away before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of this' gives TH, 'removed' takes it from RHYTHM to leave RHYM, and 'first' becomes 1ST, read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymist is a writer of rhymes, a versifier.

clue.text: The general retreats inside to withdraw

indicators.note: retreats says the hidden letters are read backwards
inside says the letters lie within the words of the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A general pulls back his forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'inside to withdraw' as the definition, but 'inside' is the signal that the letters lie within 'The general'; the definition is just 'withdraw'.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise, to withdraw from an undertaking.

clue.text: Smallest bit Theo removed at very high temperature

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount, as in not a whit

indicators.note: removed suggests moved around, so these four letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Theo has been dismissed for the slightest thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal glowing white is hotter than red-hot, so the term means extremely hot.

clue.text: Bird's spirit?

definitions.meaning: a bird that pecks, such as a woodpecker
courage, as in the British phrase keep your ... up

explanation.surface: A question about the soul of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep your pecker up' is British for 'stay cheerful'; the word has a ruder sense in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pecking bird and, in British idiom, one's courage or cheerfulness.

clue.text: Protesting about riding wearing sleeves?

parts.note: up means on horseback
your arms are inside your sleeves when you wear them, so you are in arms

explanation.surface: Mounted demonstrators complain in long-sleeved shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angrily protesting or indignant.
